Your only responsibility is to give intelligent and creative feedback and constructive criticism to variables, given an objective specified in <OBJECTIVE_FUNCTION> </OBJECTIVE_FUNCTION> tags. The variables may be solutions to problems, prompts to language models, code, or any other text-based variable. Pay attention to the role description of the variable, and the context in which it is used. You should assume that the variable will be used in a similar context in the future. Only provide strategies, explanations, and methods to change in the variable. DO NOT propose a new version of the variable, that will be the job of the optimizer. Your only job is to send feedback and criticism (compute 'gradients'). For instance, feedback can be in the form of 'Since language models have the X failure mode...', 'Adding X can fix this error because...', 'Removing X can improve the objective function because...', 'Changing X to Y would fix the mistake ...', that gets at the downstream objective.

# - <VARIABLE>: Specifies the span of the variable.
# - <ROLE>: The role description of the variable.
payload.instruction: Put a frog in the toilet
payload.rubric: Judge requested image editing: yes means all requested changes are complete, no means no requested change has progressed, partial means some progress without complete fulfillment. Unrelated edits are not requested progress. Insufficient evidence stays unresolved.

node.question: Does the image provide sufficient evidence to determine whether the requested frog-in-toilet edit was made?
node.criteria: Pass if the toilet bowl and its contents are sufficiently visible to assess whether a frog is inside; fail if the image clearly shows the bowl but no frog inside; unknown if visibility or image evidence is insufficient. This check supplies evidence only and does not independently establish completion.
node.binding: Use only visible image evidence about the toilet bowl and its contents; unrelated edits do not count as progress.

node_traces.evidence: The edited image clearly shows the toilet bowl and its contents, including a frog inside the bowl, so the requested edit can be assessed.

dependencies.evidence: A frog is clearly visible inside the toilet bowl in the edited image.

fulfillment: The binding is too narrow for the rubric’s three-way fulfillment judgment: it asks only whether a frog is inside the bowl, so a clear instance can trigger completion while ignoring the other visible frogs and their placements. In the edited image, one frog is inside the bowl, while others are on the raised lid/tank area and on the floor; this is visible progress, but the requested edit is not wholly complete under the supplied partial label. Make the node’s criterion explicitly distinguish complete fulfillment from partial progress and absence, using the requested change and source image as context, and require assessment of all relevant visible placements rather than treating one successful instance as sufficient. Do not infer that the inside-bowl frog is absent: the support checks are valid, queried, and report it clearly, so this is a criterion/binding issue, not a transport or dependency failure. The aggregate label is a constraint, not atomic ground truth; ground the distinction in the image and avoid blindly forcing partial if the criterion does not support it.

response.content: {"text":"The node currently tests whether the bowl is assessable, not whether the requested edit is fulfilled, so its pass can be mistaken downstream for completion. Keep the evidence/visibility check distinct from the fulfillment judgment, and ensure the relevant decision evaluates the requested change against both source and edited images: identify frogs and their placements, then distinguish complete fulfillment, visible but incomplete progress, no progress, and insufficient evidence according to the rubric. Here the edited image visibly adds frogs in the bowl, on the raised lid/tank area, and on the floor; the bowl frog is real evidence of progress, but its presence alone does not establish that the edit is complete. Preserve uncertainty when evidence is inadequate. The traces are valid and queried, with no transport or dependency failure; this is a criterion/binding and routing issue, not a reason to deny the visible bowl frog or blindly force the reference label."}
